model_response_en: Admittedly, critics raise a legitimate concern that autonomous robotics and generative software can displace routine clerical and assembly-line workers. During initial transition phases, rapid automation does create localized employment friction for personnel whose tasks follow rigid, codifiable rules. However, treating technological upgrading as a fixed-pie zero-sum game overlooks how productivity gains expand downstream service and engineering roles. Much as spreadsheet software eliminated manual ledger keeping while multiplying demand for financial data analysts, coupling industrial automation with subsidized reskilling programs enables displaced workers to transition into robot fleet supervision, calibration, and exception handling.
